name: Kochi · Kerala
tagline: Spice port, fishing nets and the Kerala backwaters
summary: Kochi's Fort Kochi quarter blends Portuguese, Dutch, British and Jewish history with spice warehouses, art cafés and the giant Chinese fishing nets. It is the gateway to Kerala's backwaters, where houseboats drift through palm-lined canals.
seasonNote: November to March is dry and warm. The southwest monsoon (June to September) is heavy but lush, and good for Ayurvedic treatments. The Kochi-Muziris Biennale art festival runs from December every other year.
arrival: Cochin International Airport is about an hour from Fort Kochi; trains arrive at Ernakulam.
gettingAround: Walk or cycle Fort Kochi; ferries cross to Ernakulam; the metro covers the mainland.
cashTip: UPI and cards are common; carry some cash for ferries and stalls.
foodTip: Kerala fish curry, karimeen pearl-spot fried in banana leaf, appam with stew, and sadya feasts on banana leaves.
buyTip: Spices from Mattancherry's warehouses, Kerala tea, coir crafts and antiques on Jew Town Road.
baseArea: Fort Kochi heritage homestays and hotels
